Financial wellbeing for teachers
Protection before growth

Life insurance protects income

Start with the financial impact of losing an income.

Who needs it?

Anyone whose family depends on their income or future contribution.

What to understand?

Understand pure protection and keep investment objectives clear.

How to think?

Income replacement, liabilities and future goals.

Discussion

Investment or safety net?

Protection-gap illustration

Simple protection gap₹1.00 crSimplified gap: expenses × years + commitments − available assets/cover. Excludes inflation and investment growth; avoid counting assets reserved for other goals.
Insurance is a risk-transfer tool, not a guaranteed wealth-building shortcut.07

Small instalments. A long-term plan.

Change one assumption at a time and discuss what happens.

Beginning-of-month deposits. Annual return assumption ÷ 12, compounded monthly. SIP increases after every 12 deposits. Assumption is net of recurring fund expenses; taxes and exit loads excluded. Actual market paths may include losses.

Compare a flat SIP with the increased SIP at the same assumed rate. Higher contributions also explain the difference.

Financial wellbeing for teachers

What could your retirement income gap be?

An adjustable illustration—not a retirement recommendation.

Future budget = today’s budget × (1 + inflation)^years. Illustrative corpus = first-year annual income gap ÷ chosen initial withdrawal rate. This is a rough scenario, not a safe-withdrawal rule.

Why this is only a starting estimate

The ratio does not model longevity, changing expenses, future returns, taxes, withdrawal order, pension escalation or medical shocks. A 4% illustration is not a guarantee that money will last. Existing retirement assets must be projected separately before estimating an additional saving requirement.
